picks.rationale: Both starting pitchers are in excellent form for this matchup; Eduardo Rodriguez of the Diamondbacks holds a 2.64 ERA, while Jared Jones of the Pirates has a 3.72 ERA and has allowed three runs or fewer in his last four starts. The head-to-head history strongly supports a low-scoring game, with the Under hitting in 7 of the last 9 meetings between these teams and 3 of 5 this season. Given the strong pitching and historical trends, the low total of 5.5 is well-justified for this contest.

The Washington Nationals are in strong recent form, having won their last three games and scoring 23 runs in that span. They face a Toronto Blue Jays team that ranks 30th in the league for runs scored this season and is dealing with a potential injury to Vladimir Guerrero Jr.. Nationals' starter Zack Littell has been effective, allowing two earned runs or fewer in four of his last five outings, while Blue Jays' starter Trey Yesavage has given up three or more earned runs in his last three starts. This combination of offensive disparity, pitching advantage, and Blue Jays' injury concerns makes the Nationals a confident pick to cover the spread.

The San Diego Padres are playing well, having won their last three games and holding a dominant 4-1 record in their last five head-to-head matchups against the Rockies. The Colorado Rockies have struggled on the road with a 25-30 record and have lost five of their last seven games overall. Padres' starter Griffin Canning has a respectable 3.68 ERA over 11 starts, providing a solid foundation against a struggling Rockies lineup. Playing at home where they are 27-24, the Padres are in a strong position to secure a multi-run victory.

The Tampa Bay Rays boast a strong 62-44 overall record and a superior team ERA of 3.51 compared to the Rangers' 4.30. Texas Rangers' starter MacKenzie Gore has been in poor form, posting a 1-2 record with a high 7.66 ERA in his five July starts. While Rays' starter Ian Seymour's numbers are modest, he has performed serviceably at home. The Rays' overall team strength and the Rangers' starting pitcher's recent struggles provide a clear edge for Tampa Bay to win by more than one run.

The Cincinnati Reds enter this game with better recent form, holding a 6-4 record in their last 10 games, while the Guardians are 3-7 in the same span. Reds' starting pitcher Brady Singer has demonstrated a significant home-field advantage, boasting a 2.98 ERA when pitching in Cincinnati, a marked improvement over his overall 4.53 ERA. Conversely, Guardians' starter Joey Cantillo has struggled on the road this season. These factors, combined with the Reds' recent win in a head-to-head matchup, make them a strong value play at home.
